title: Hibachi Fried Rice with Yum Yum Sauce

items: 4 cups cooked white rice, chilled at least 12 hr (from about 1⅓ cups uncooked)
1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into ¾-inch pieces, or 1 lb peeled deveined shrimp
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Whisk the sauce ingredients together, adding water until it pours like heavy cream. Chill while you cook.
Break up the cold rice with your hands so there are no clumps.

Heat the oil and 1 Tbsp butter in the skillet over medium-high heat. Add the protein, season with salt, pepper and 1 Tbsp soy sauce and cook until the chicken reads 165°F (5–7 min) or the shrimp are pink and opaque (2–3 min). Move it to a plate.
Add 1 Tbsp butter, the onion and the peas and carrots. Cook 3–4 min, stirring, until the onion softens.
Add the rice, the remaining 2 Tbsp butter, the garlic and 2 Tbsp soy sauce. Spread it out and cook 4–5 min, turning it every minute, until hot and starting to crisp.
Push the rice to one side. Pour the eggs into the empty spot and scramble about 1 min, until set, then stir them into the rice.
Return the protein and its juices and toss 1 min to heat through. Serve with the yum yum sauce drizzled over the top in lines.
tips: Use rice cooked the day before and chilled. Fresh rice turns mushy. In a pinch, spread fresh rice on a sheet pan and refrigerate 30 min uncovered.
If your pan is small, cook the rice in 2 batches. A crowded pan steams the rice instead of frying it.
The sauce tastes better after an hour in the fridge, so make it first or the day before.
storage: Cool leftover fried rice within 2 hr and refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat with a splash of water, or microwave covered until steaming hot (165°F). The sauce keeps 1 week in the fridge.
